newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank key rate seen up by June 1998 - poll.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank key rate seen up by June 1998 - poll.

text.p: The Bank of Finland's tender rate is forecast to remain unchanged at 3.00 percent in the next three months, but a majority of respondents in a Reuters poll expect a hike by June 1998.
Of the 23 dealers, economists and analysts at banks and corporate treasuries polled, 22 expected the central bank to keep the tender rate on hold until end-August.
One saw scope for a 50 basis points hike before September.
But looking one year ahead, the tender rate was expected to move higher, with the median of forecasts at 3.28 percent, in a 3.00 to 4.50 percent range. The mean stood at 3.39 percent. @

Five banks and one corporate treasury expected the central bank to keep the tender rate unchanged at 3.00 percent throughout the coming 12 months, while 10 respondents saw the tender rate rising to above 3.50 percent within one year.
Six respondents expected the tender rate to be between 3.00 percent and 3.50 percent by June 1998.
One market operator saw a 150 basis points hike to 4.50 percent by June next year.
The quarterly poll was conducted by telephone on May 22-23. The forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis.
The Bank of Finland's tender rate at 3.00 percent has been on par with the German repo rate since October.

Forecasts by: Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd., Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), Enso, Handelsbaken Markets Finland, Huhtamaki Finance, I.D.E.A. (London), Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Kesko, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SE-Banken Helsinki, SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
